rows.question: Why can the same 30-day fill cost more at a standard pharmacy than a preferred one on this plan?
rows.answer: On this MAPD plan, preferred retail and standard retail are different cost-share categories, so the same 30-day medication can have a lower member cost at a preferred pharmacy and a higher cost at a standard pharmacy. For the recorded 30-day metformin 500 mg fills, the plan rule lists $8 at preferred retail and $27 at standard retail; it reflects the pharmacy’s network classification on the fill date, not a change in the prescription.

rows.answer: Enrollment itself does not place a fill, start automatic refills, or change today’s retail pickup; retail can remain an option. The existing prescription can support an eligible 90-day supply, and medications can be selected individually, so enrolling does not require moving atorvastatin or both medicines.
